parsed.n_justification: A one-factor controlled sweep of clay content from 5% to 55% in ~10% increments yields 6 discrete levels (5, 15, 25, 35, 45, 55%). All columns share identical location, forcing, and non-clay parameters so that clay is the sole varied factor. Six levels adequately resolve the monotonic-to-nonlinear partitioning response without excessive redundancy.
requires_capabilities: User-defined surface dataset (fsurdat) or namelist override to prescribe PCT_CLAY and PCT_SAND per soil layer
Model spin-up capability (accelerated or extended) to equilibrate soil moisture and water table before analysis
assumptions: All columns use identical location, meteorological forcing, vegetation/PFT, slope, and soil depth so clay content is the only varied factor.
Clay is varied uniformly across all soil layers; sand and silt are adjusted to sum to 100% following the texture triangle noted per column.
Default ELM pedotransfer functions (Clapp-Hornberger / Cosby) map texture to hydraulic properties; no macropore or preferential-flow parameterization added.
First ~10 years treated as spin-up; partitioning analysis uses the remaining quasi-equilibrium period.
Recharge is diagnosed from QDRAI/QRECHARGE (bottom drainage to aquifer) and runoff from QOVER/QRUNOFF; their ratio characterizes partitioning.
Chosen site (Konza-like central US grassland, ~39.1N, -96.6W) provides a moderate precipitation regime suitable for exposing runoff/recharge sensitivity; conceptual so exact location is illustrative.
No lateral inflow; single-column 1D vertical water balance assumed.
